title: Precise words give expectations proportion

captions.physics: Conveying a promise through uncertain wording
captions.energy: Matching expectations to words actually accepted
captions.emotions: Feeling proportion between reply and commitment

meaning: You can convey a promise through uncertain wording and match expectations to words actually accepted, feeling proportion between reply and commitment without proving the other person wrong.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Moon in the physical position can appear in uncertain wording instead of a precise promise. Justice in energy supports a wish to match expectations to words actually accepted. Justice in emotions brings proportion between an answer and a commitment. Motivation to clarify scope differs from feeling the correspondence found. You can clarify what was promised without turning difference into an argument about whose expectation deserves more.

Suppose conversation includes “I will try to answer today”, later remembered that evening as a promise to finish the entire discussion. You can distinguish trying to reply from undertaking to exhaust the subject. **A promise’s scope depends on what was actually accepted**. It becomes possible to name the response expected and what remains unready now. Proportion allows frustration to be taken seriously without making it evidence of a broken word. The original ambiguity requires neither dismissing every request nor promising more for reconciliation.

Difficulty arises if this precision becomes grounds never to discuss the other person’s disappointment. Correspondence to words replaces a living response to a request. Constructive Justice helps distinguish commitment’s scope from a feeling’s significance while preserving room for both. You can decline an expanded promise and hear an expectation carefully; fair clarity requires neither identical feelings about delay nor a final verdict on either person’s reliability.
